entries.46d81a7d7ebcfcc4: The Kubota Group consists of the company and 207 affiliates in Japan and overseas (190 consolidated subsidiaries and 17 equity-method affiliates), and provides a wide variety of products and services across three business segments: Machinery, Water & Environment, and Other. The three business segments are largely consistent with the organizational structure divided based on products and services, and the chief operating decision maker regularly reviews their operating results to decide resource allocation and assess performance. The main sources of revenue are Machinery and Water & Environment. In Machinery, revenue is recognized when agricultural machinery, engines and construction machinery are delivered to dealers or end users. In Water & Environment, in addition to product sales, it undertakes construction contracts for public facilities such as environmental facilities and waterworks facilities, and revenue for construction is recognized as work progresses. For customers buying machinery, the group's retail finance companies provide leases and installment sales, and their interest income and insurance income are included in 'revenue recognized from other sources.' The company sets its future vision as becoming a 'Global Major Brand (GMB),' that is, a company able to contribute the most to society by being trusted by the most customers, and under its long-term vision 'GMB2030,' looking ahead to 2030, it has set out a 'platformer supporting life' committed to a rich society and the circulation of nature. The consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards, and in the trend of key management indicators, the line between revenue and net income is 'profit before tax.'

entries.4a7d2ee7e92e5e36: This is a business segment that manufactures and sells agricultural machinery and agriculture-related products, engines, construction machinery, and so on. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥2,628,618 million (down 0.3% year on year), accounting for 87.1% of total revenue; including intersegment revenue, the total was ¥2,628,861 million; segment profit was ¥253,638 million (down 21.6% year on year); and the number of employees was 41,342, the largest of the three business segments. Domestic revenue rose 13.8% year on year to ¥354.8 billion, driven by an increase in agricultural machinery and agriculture-related products, while overseas revenue fell 2.2% year on year to ¥2,273.8 billion. The company cites higher costs due to the impact of U.S. tariffs, losses from reduced sales, and a deterioration in sales mix as reasons for the decline in segment profit. This business also includes retail finance provided by Kubota Credit Co., Ltd., Kubota Credit Corp.,U.S.A., Siam Kubota Leasing Co.,Ltd., and Kubota (Chūgoku) Yūshi Soryō Yūgen Kōsha.

entries.51c98e5bc46c0b4d: It handles agricultural machinery such as tractors, tillers, combine harvesters, rice transplanters, lawn mowers and utility vehicles, as well as implements, attachments, post-harvest equipment, vegetable machinery, intermediate-management machines, mini rice centers, seedling-raising, rice-milling and horticultural facilities, and various weighing, measuring and control equipment and systems. For the farm operations support system 'KSAS,' the 'KSAS AI chat function,' which uses generative AI, and the 'satellite remote sensing function,' which displays crop growth conditions on a map using satellite images, were developed. The range of models equipped with the 'GS (straight-line automatic steering) function,' which enables automatic straight-line travel and work using position information from satellite positioning systems, is being expanded to tractors, combine harvesters, rice transplanters and riding automatic vegetable transplanters.
entries.528995db52438418: It handles construction machinery and related products, such as mini backhoes, wheel loaders, compact track loaders and skid-steer loaders. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥625,311 million. In North America, the market remained firm owing to stable housing and public works markets; however, because current-year demand returned to a level in line with demand, compared with the previous year's inventory-replenishment demand, sales declined, while in Europe, sales increased owing to a market recovery. The company positions the construction machinery business as one of three growth pillars of the Machinery Business, alongside the India-origin business and the Lifecycle Support business.
entries.5483ce7e52c6f304: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥265,470 million, a decrease of ¥50.2 billion (15.9%) from the previous year. The company cites higher costs associated with the impact of U.S. tariffs, sales reduction losses in the Machinery segment and a deterioration in sales mix as the main reasons for the decline, while stating that cost absorption is progressing well through reduced incentives, price revisions and lower fixed costs. Segment profit by business was ¥253,638 million for Machinery, ¥32,983 million for Water & Environment, ¥824 million for Other and adjustments of -¥21,975 million, and the total matches operating profit in the consolidated statement of income. Profit before tax was ¥282,140 million (down 15.9% from the previous year), income tax expense was ¥68.1 billion, equity-method investment income was ¥2.7 billion, and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥186,687 million (down 19.0% year on year).
